stem.text: A particle moves in the xy-plane so that its position at time t is \( \left(x(t), y(t)\right) = \left( - \frac{t^{3}}{3} + 2 t,\ - \frac{t^{2}}{2} + 3 \sin{\left(t \right)} + 6 \right) \) for \( 0 \le t \le 2 \). For \( 0 \le t \le 2 \), \( y(t) > 0 \). Using a calculator where needed, find all times t in the open interval \( 0 < t < 2 \) at which the particle is moving toward the x-axis. Give a reason for your answer, and give any decimal endpoint correct to three decimal places.

answer_key.label: The particle moves toward the x-axis for \( 1.170 < t < 2 \), because \( y(t) \) and \( y'(t) \) have opposite signs there.

worked_solution.text: The stem gives \( y(t) > 0 \) on the whole interval, so the particle stays on one side of the x-axis.

The particle moves toward the x-axis when \( y(t) \) and \( y'(t) \) have opposite signs, that is, when \( y'(t) = - t + 3 \cos{\left(t \right)} < 0 \). A calculator gives \( y'(t) = 0 \) at \( t \approx 1.170 \), with \( y'(t) \) positive before that time and the opposite sign after it.
So the particle moves toward the x-axis for \( 1.170 < t < 2 \), because there \( y(t) > 0 \) and \( y'(t) < 0 \), so its distance from the x-axis, \( |y(t)| \), is decreasing.
worked_solution.rule_named: sign analysis of the velocity component

The particle moves toward the x-axis for \( \sqrt{2} < t < 2 \), because \( x'(t) \) is negative there.
